accuracy.evidence: The standards were checked against the Common Core text: RL.K.9 (with prompting, compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in familiar stories), RL.1.9 (compare and contrast the adventures and experiences of characters in stories) and RL.2.9 (compare two or more versions of the same story), plus RI.1.9 and RI.2.9 for two texts on one topic; the National Curriculum in England Years 1 and 2 reading comprehension aims (discuss, link to other books, explain understanding). Both stories were written for this lesson, so every fact, proof line, same/different answer and true/not-true claim was checked line by line against the text shown on screen (for example, only Pip's hat goes in the pond; Mo's helper is his sister, a person).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-comparison slips: saying both when only one text fits (truth step: both stories are about a kite, both helpers are animals; mastery m5; practice p5), lumping similar answers (sad vs cross: step 3 prediction, judge feedback, m7), crossing details between texts (Mo's sister helping Pip: challenge 'mixed', m1), giving one text's evidence for a both claim (proof step needs a line from each; challenge 'oneproof'), and misusing but for a similarity or both in the wrong place (join step, challenge 'butsame' and 'bothplace').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtwotale is built on two texts at once: a three-part Only Mo / Both / Only Pip sort with feedback that quotes the line from each story, a proof step where a both claim is only accepted once a line is tapped in each story column, a same-or-different judgment with the two answers side by side, a both/but/too sentence join, and a true-for-both check. The single-story labs (flagsmap story map, flagtrait character traits, flagview viewpoints) never hold two texts side by side. lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rules by doing: putting 'Gets help' in Only Mo returns 'Gets help? Mo: "His big sister got a ladder." Pip: "Frog swam out and got it." So it goes in Both', and tapping the wrong Pip line returns 'that line does not show that. Look for the line where Pip gets help'. Choosing Same for sad and cross returns 'Sad and cross are both bad feelings, but they are not the same feeling.' The done screens list every claim with its two proof lines and every compare sentence in full.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions each carry a tempting wrong answer the step then disproves: that a boy and a duck are too different to have alike stories (the sort puts three facts in Both), that only Mo gets help (the proof step finds Frog), that sad and cross are the same feeling because both are bad (the same/different step), and that both shows a difference (the join step shows but does). The done line repeats the child's prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with eleven distinct wrong-answer messages: only Mo has a kite, only Mo has a sister, 'both feel bad' is a likeness not a difference, both vs but, crossing Mo's helper into Pip's story, only the hat gets wet, only the kite goes up a tree, Frog is an animal but the sister is a person, one story's line cannot prove a both claim, but for a match, and both at the end of a sentence where too belongs.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs are short and concrete (Ask the same question about both. What do they lose? Mo loses a kite. Pip loses a hat. That is different.) and pass the family readability limit in validate_lessons. The two stories are five and six lines of simple sentences shown as real HTML text under the canvas, so they can be read aloud by a parent or a screen reader; the adult text names the standards and the Venn organiser.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases and the explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including Characters, Settings and Events, Character Traits and Motivation and Characters' Viewpoints and Responses. Every feedback line quotes the story or names the specific slip; step texts are one rule and one instruction.

mobile.evidence: Checked all six steps at 360 px with touch in light and dark, before and after Show me. The Venn boxes show sorted facts as separate white chips, the proof step fits five Mo and six Pip sentence cards in two columns after shortening the last line, the side-by-side answer cards and Same/Different keys fit with room to tap, and the both/but/too tiles are 56 px tall. The story text block is hidden on the proof step, where the stories are already on the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate completed all five tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a labelled button ('Gets help: Both', 'Pip, line 5: Frog swam out and got it.', 'What takes it? Same', 'Fill the gap with but', 'Both helpers are animals. Not true'); the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback line, and the stories are an ordered list in two labelled sections with no custom colours.

sources: Common Core State Standards ELA: RL.K.9, RL.1.9, RL.2.9 (compare and contrast characters' adventures and experiences) and RI.1.9, RI.2.9 (two texts on the same topic)
